claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an approximately single-phase BCC microstructure.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Replacing Hf with V to form Hf0.8V0.2MoTaTiZr will reduce density by approximately 10% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Hf0.8V0.2MoTaTiZr will retain room-temperature yield strength within ±5% of approximately 1600 MPa.
Hf0.8V0.2MoTaTiZr will retain yield strength at 1000 °C within ±5% of approximately 855 MPa.
Conventional induction melting followed by as-cast processing can produce homogeneous Hf0.8V0.2MoTaTiZr.
The modified Hf0.8V0.2MoTaTiZr alloy will retain a single-phase BCC structure.
Substitution of Hf by V will increase lattice distortion because of atomic-size mismatch between Hf and V.
Replacing heavy Hf with lighter V lowers the alloy's overall density.
Hf–V size-mismatch-induced lattice distortion will provide solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed solid-solution strengthening will compensate for the Hf substitution and preserve yield strength at both room temperature and 1000 °C.

contradictions.description: The prose says that approximately 20 at.% of Hf is replaced by V, which ordinarily denotes an absolute 20 at.% substitution, whereas normalized Hf0.8V0.2MoTaTiZr contains only 4 at.% V and 16 at.% Hf. The formula instead represents replacement of 20% of the original Hf inventory.
